# Auth Emails — Light Theme via Resend

## Context

The signup confirmation email (screenshotted 2026-05-20) renders in dark mode:
white turtle logo on near-black card, with light gray body text. That email is
**not** generated by this codebase — it is sent by Supabase Auth using the
"Confirm signup" template configured in the Supabase Dashboard
(Auth → Email Templates).

Every other transactional email in the app already renders light via Resend +
[lib/email/templates.ts](lib/email/templates.ts) (`bgLight: #ffffff`,
`bgGray: #f8f9fa`, dark navy footer). The brand standard for email is light; the
dark Supabase-hosted template is the lone outlier and breaks brand consistency.

This plan converts the remaining auth flows that still rely on Supabase-hosted
templates so that **every** auth email is rendered from `lib/email/templates.ts`
and sent through Resend. After this lands, the Supabase-hosted templates are
only ever rendered if someone calls a non-admin auth method we missed — which
this plan removes.

Reference patterns already in the repo:
- [app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts](app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts) — canonical pattern: `admin.generateLink({ type: 'recovery' })` + `sendPasswordResetEmail`.
- [app/api/auth/send-login-link/route.ts](app/api/auth/send-login-link/route.ts) — same pattern for `type: 'magiclink'` + `sendMagicLoginEmail`.
- [lib/email/send.ts:1182](lib/email/send.ts#L1182) — `sendConfirmationEmail()` already exists, light theme, EN/JP. Wired up but never called.
- [lib/email/send.ts:1360](lib/email/send.ts#L1360) — `sendMagicLoginEmail()`, light theme.

## Scope

In: Signup confirm + signup resend (the screenshotted bug), partner-thanks magic
link, plus a one-line dashboard task to neutralize the four Supabase-hosted
templates as a belt-and-suspenders measure.

Out: Email-change confirmation (no UI in the app today triggers `updateUser({ email })` — flag for a later plan when that feature lands). Invite-user (Supabase `inviteUserByEmail` is not called anywhere in the codebase; admin onboarding already uses `admin.createUser` + custom Resend welcome emails via `lib/students/actions.ts` and `lib/instructors/actions.ts`, both of which already use light templates).

## Files to create

### `app/api/auth/signup/route.ts` (new)

POST `{ email, password, fullName, locale, redirectTo }` → returns
`{ ok, needsConfirmation }`. Server-side flow:

1. Rate-limit by IP (mirror [forgot-password route](app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts) — no bucket today, but signup is a write op so add a 10/hr/IP token bucket using the same pattern as [send-login-link](app/api/auth/send-login-link/route.ts#L28-L46)).
2. `adminClient.auth.admin.createUser({ email, password, email_confirm: false, user_metadata: { full_name } })`. This creates the auth user **without** sending Supabase's hosted confirmation email.
3. If `createUser` returns "User already exists" → return `{ ok: true, alreadyExists: true }` (caller shows the same "check your email" UI to prevent enumeration; do not send).
4. `adminClient.auth.admin.generateLink({ type: 'signup', email, password, options: { redirectTo: \`${origin}/api/auth/callback?redirect=${encodeURIComponent(redirectTo)}\` } })` to mint the confirm action_link.
5. `await sendConfirmationEmail({ email, fullName, confirmLink: linkData.properties.action_link, locale })` — function already exists at [lib/email/send.ts:1182](lib/email/send.ts#L1182).
6. Return `{ ok: true, needsConfirmation: true }`.

Errors from Resend send are logged and swallowed (consistent with forgot-password). The auth user is still created either way; the user can request a resend.

### `app/api/auth/resend-confirmation/route.ts` (new)

POST `{ email, locale, redirectTo }` → returns `{ ok: true }`.

1. Same 10/hr/IP rate limit bucket.
2. `adminClient.auth.admin.generateLink({ type: 'signup', email, options: { redirectTo: ... } })`. The current SDK requires `password` for `type: 'signup'` even on regenerate — pass a throwaway since the row already exists (Supabase ignores it for users that already exist; if it complains, fall back to `type: 'magiclink'` which also confirms the email on click).
3. `await sendConfirmationEmail(...)` with the same light template.
4. Always return 200 to prevent enumeration.

## Files to modify

### [components/auth/AuthForm.tsx](components/auth/AuthForm.tsx#L122-L175)

Replace the direct Supabase calls with `fetch`-based calls to the new routes.

- **Lines 127–147** (`mode === 'sign-up'` branch): swap `supabase.auth.signUp(...)` for `await fetch('/api/auth/signup', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ email, password, fullName, locale, redirectTo }) })`. Read `{ ok, needsConfirmation }`; on success set `confirmationPending = true`. The signed-up user is **never** auto-logged-in by this flow now (Supabase used to return a session in some configs), so always show the "check your email" screen.
- **Lines 261–280** (resend confirmation button): swap `supabase.auth.resend({ type: 'signup', ... })` for `await fetch('/api/auth/resend-confirmation', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ email, locale, redirectTo }) })`.

Keep the existing UI states (`confirmationPending`, `confirmationFailed`,
`resending`) and copy as-is.

### [app/api/auth/magic-link/route.ts:138-159](app/api/auth/magic-link/route.ts#L138-L159)

The partner-thanks magic-link route currently relies on the (incorrect) comment
that "Supabase auto-sends." Per
[send-login-link/route.ts:87-89](app/api/auth/send-login-link/route.ts#L87-L89),
`admin.generateLink` does **not** send the email. Two possibilities:

- If Supabase is currently sending its hosted "Magic Link" template here, it's dark like the confirm email.
- If Supabase isn't sending at all, paying partners are getting no email after checkout — a worse bug.

Either way: mirror `send-login-link/route.ts`. After `generateLink`, look up
`full_name` from `users` and call `sendMagicLoginEmail({ email, fullName,
loginLink: data.properties.action_link, locale })`. Remove the stale comment
block at lines 154–157.

## Supabase Dashboard step (do this once after deploy)

Auth → Email Templates → set the message body of **Confirm signup**, **Magic
Link**, **Invite user**, and **Change Email Address** to a single sentence that
will never be seen by a real user — e.g.:

```
This email is not used. If you received this message, contact help@honuvibe.com.
```

This is a defense-in-depth measure. Once the code changes ship, none of these
templates should fire from any flow we control — but neutering them prevents a
future regression from silently shipping a dark email.

Do **not** disable signups at the project level; we still rely on Supabase's
`createUser` admin API to create rows in `auth.users`.

## Verification

End-to-end on the dev server (`pnpm dev`), in a private window so cookies don't
leak between tests:

1. **Signup (EN):** Go to `/learn/auth`, switch to "Sign up", register with a
   `+test1@` alias on Ryan's address. Confirm:
   - Browser shows "Check your email" UI.
   - Inbox: subject is `Confirm your email — HonuVibe.AI`. Email renders **light** (white card on light-gray background, navy footer, teal "Confirm Email Address →" button).
   - Click the link → lands on dashboard, session active.
2. **Signup (JP):** `/ja/learn/auth`, register with `+test2@`. Confirm:
   - Email subject is `【HonuVibe.AI】メールアドレスの確認`. JP body, light theme, JP-tuned line-height (Noto Sans JP rendered by Outlook fallback chain).
3. **Resend confirmation:** From the "Check your email" screen, click "Resend confirmation email". A second copy of the same light email arrives.
4. **Magic link via partner thanks:** Complete a Stripe test-mode checkout for any partner SKU. On the thanks page, the magic-link email should arrive (light, `Your login link — HonuVibe.AI`). Before this plan, this flow may have been silently broken; this verifies the side-fix.
5. **Forgot password (regression check):** Trigger `/learn/auth` → "Forgot password" → confirm email is still light (no change expected, but the dashboard template change should not break it because `forgot-password` already uses Resend).
6. **No duplicate emails:** For each of #1–#4, confirm only **one** email arrives per action. If two arrive, the Supabase-hosted template is still firing — re-check the dashboard step.

Smoke test build and types:

```
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build
```

If `auth.admin.generateLink({ type: 'signup' })` throws a TypeScript error on
missing `password` (per the PROGRESS.md note at line 1709), pass the original
signup password through to the new route and forward it; do not weaken the type
or use `as any`.

## Risk notes

- `admin.createUser({ email_confirm: false })` does not enforce password strength rules — Supabase's `signUp()` did. Add a minimum-length check (≥8 chars) in the new `/api/auth/signup` route to match the prior UX. The AuthForm already enforces this client-side; mirror it server-side for safety.
- The new signup route runs with the service role key — keep it server-only (`route.ts`), never imported into client components.
- Rate limit bucket is in-memory (resets per cold start, leaks across instances). Same trade-off as the other auth routes; acceptable because the abuse ceiling is bounded by Resend send quotas and the email confirmation requirement.
